Forensics.text: A file that doesn't look quite right has been left behind. Sometimes, the first step in solving a mystery is simply asking: what exactly am I looking at?
Forensics.hint: Don't judge a file by its extension. Let the MIME type speak.
Forensics.subtitle: The Forged Manifest

Reverse Engineering.text: Solve the Reverse Engineering challenge and submit your flag.
Reverse Engineering.hint: There are way too many complex equations in this binary to solve by hand or brute force. Try using   			  an advanced solver script like the Z3 Theorem Prover, or a symbolic execution framework like Angr to 			  find the mathematical path to success.
Reverse Engineering.subtitle: Ghost Mechanism

Web Exploitation.text: We stumbled upon the new Employee Portal for CoreDump Corp. They claim their new architecture is incredibly secure and that employees can only view their own notes. See if you can prove them wrong and uncover the admin's secret.
Web Exploitation.subtitle: The Governor's Vault

OSINT.text: A familiar car wash hides more than just dirty cars. Somewhere behind the business is a lawyer, and your job is to uncover his real name and phone number using publicly available information.
OSINT.hint: Start with the car wash. Follow the trail through public records and business information.  Flag Format: coredump{abc_xyz_123_456}
OSINT.subtitle: Follow the Trail

Steganography.text: This image looks innocent enough... but there's more hiding inside it than what meets the eye. Dig into its metadata and investigate what the image may be concealing.
Steganography.hint: Start by examining the image's metadata. If that doesn't reveal everything, look for something hidden within the file itself.
Steganography.subtitle: Message in a Bottle

Binary Analysis.text: One of our highly secure production servers experienced a fatal hardware failure and crashed. We managed to extract the executable and the resulting core memory dump. We believe the secret encryption flag was loaded into memory right before the crash. Since the binary is stripped, can you dive into the memory dump and find it?
Binary Analysis.hint: The 'strings' command won't save you here because the flag isn't stored as continuous text in        			  memory. Load the core dump into GDB along with the executable, figure out where the data was loaded, 			  and inspect the raw memory registers to pull out the raw hex values.
Binary Analysis.subtitle: Sunken Registers

Miscellaneous.text: My friend hid the flag somewhere inside a pile of complete gibberish — and then encoded the entire thing. Can you work your way through the mess and find what was hidden?
Miscellaneous.hint: The gibberish isn't the only thing you need to decode. Sometimes, one layer of encoding leads to another.
Miscellaneous.subtitle: Dead Man's Switch

Miscellaneous 2.text: I asked a cow for the flag, but all it gave me was a strange sequence of moos in two different tones. Maybe the cow is trying to tell you something...
Miscellaneous 2.hint: Two different tones. Two different symbols. Think about a code that only needs two states.
Miscellaneous 2.subtitle: The Bovine Cipher

Pwn.text: We managed to get a copy of the company's secure chat portal executable. It's heavily protected by modern memory mitigations (Stack Canaries). Can you find a way to bypass the protections and access the secret admin function to reveal the flag?
Pwn.hint: The 'gets()' function gives you a classic buffer overflow, but the Stack Canary will crash the       			  program before you can win. Notice how the program prints back your alias? Try entering format       			  string specifiers (like %15$p) to leak the secret Canary off the stack so you can perfectly place it 			  back during your overflow.
Pwn.subtitle: Walk the Plank

OSINT 2.text: 9 years ago, during the first quarter of the year, a traveler named Clemens visited a restaurant somewhere in the Caribbean. Before leaving, he wrote an online review describing his experience. 		He described the location as gorgeous and surrounded by the Caribbean Sea, but wasn't impressed with the service or the food considering the price. 		During his visit, Clemens also purchased a drink. 		Your task is to identify the restaurant he visited, find the drink he ordered, and determine how much it cost in Dominican pesos.
OSINT 2.hint: Hint: Don’t focus only on the text—the information linked to the image may lead you to the answer. 		Flag Format : coredump{restaurantname_drinkname_priceinnumbers}
OSINT 2.subtitle: The Caribbean Log

Networking.text: We intercepted a strange ping sweep on our network. It looks like normal diagnostic traffic, but our intrusion detection system flagged a weird payload signature. Can you extract the hidden data?
Networking.hint: I am always before your eyes, but you scan right past me.
Networking.subtitle: Siren's Call

Cryptography.text: Two messages were encrypted using the exact same One-Time Pad (OTP) key.  			We know the plaintext of the first message is: 			"The weather in London is terrible today."  			- transmission1.hex contains the encrypted first message. 			- transmission2.hex contains the encrypted flag.  			Recover the flag from transmission2.hex.
Cryptography.hint: [ Transmission 1 = Plaintext 1 ⊕ Key ] , [ Transmission 2 = Plaintext 2 ⊕ Key ]
Cryptography.subtitle: Cipher Chest
